messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] segmentation approach methSeg
parts:
check fastSeg documentation, which is not great (https://www.rdocumentation.org/packages/fastseg/versions/1.18.0/topics/fastseg). Here are some more details from personal communication with the package maintainer, Gunter Klambauer:


"You test minInt (=minSeg) values left of the breakpoint against minInt values right of the breakpoint. Then you extend until you test maxInt values left and maxInt values right. So, if you have minInt=3 and maxInt=200, you have 197 tests and you pick the best p-value of all these tests.

Delta is a speed-up parameter: If the p-value does not get better for "delta" consecutive extension steps, then i stop this loop.

The test that is performed is the cyber t-test of Pierre Baldi. This test has a parameter "nu" (in the paper) and in my implementation "cyberWeight". This parameter is something like the "number of pseudo-points from the whole distribution" that you include in each t-test."
